booking.note: Verbatim: 'campsites can, and should be, reserved until 11pm ET on the date of arrival' and 'Indiana is 100% reservable until 11pm ET on the day of arrival' - no sites are held back for walk-ins. Walk-in registration is still accepted on the day of arrival only, with the camper present, but is being phased out and guarantees nothing. Weekend rule: a Friday night must include Thursday or Saturday; a Saturday night must include Friday or Sunday. The One-Night Relaxed Rule waives that for sites still unrented 3 days out, but 'Required holiday minimum stays are excluded from this relaxed rule' - hence two rules, not one.

fees.note: The $15/$7 figure is the park ENTRANCE fee (out-of-state / Indiana plates), not a camping surcharge - Indiana has no non-resident camping rate. For CAMPERS it is effectively once per stay, not daily: 'when staying overnight, you will be required to pay the entrance fee the first time you enter and your receipt or hang tag will serve as your in/out pass the remainder of your stay.' Exceptions: Prophetstown $8/$16, Indiana Dunes $7/$20. A Non-Resident Annual Entrance Pass is $120. FIRSTHAND (AWH, 2026): booking online charges the campsite fee, tax and the $6 reservation fee, and the $15 entrance fee is then collected AT THE GATE on arrival with no mention of it during booking. So the booking total understates a one-night out-of-state stay by 15 dollars - which is why entrance is a separate field and must be added to any quoted cost rather than assumed included. --AWH/--Claude

booking.source: https://indianastateparks.reserveamerica.com/brands/in/htm/CAMPING_BUSINESS_RULES.pdf (Minimum Stay, Maximum Stay, Minimum Booking Window, Walk-In Registrations, Opening Maximum Window)

fees.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/rates-and-fees/entrance-fees/ plus the $6 transaction fee in CAMPING_BUSINESS_RULES.pdf; per-stay hang-tag rule and the at-the-gate collection confirmed firsthand by AWH 2026

booking.note: Flagship campgrounds (marked with * on the fees page) are 'premier facilities that provide premium amenities and New York State's premier scenic attractions' and carry a $3.00/night surcharge, carried in fees.surcharges.premium_site.

fees.note: Verbatim: 'Non-NY State residents will pay an additional $5.00 per night fee at camping locations.' PER NIGHT, not per stay. Cabins/yurts differ ($7.00/night or $28/week). NY has no resident/non-resident split on park entrance. Full per-night amenity schedule: Platform/Pad $3, Weekend/Holiday $4, XL Site+ $5, Waterfront $6, Electric 15/20/30A $7, Electric 50A $9, Oceanfront $10, Full Hook-up 30A $13, Full Hook-up 50A $15 - surcharges above carries the 30A figures, the 50A ones are +$2 each. HITHER HILLS IS NOT COVERED BY THIS ROW: it doubles the nightly rate for non-residents instead, and carries its own entry-level override.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day

booking.note: CUTOFF UNRESOLVED - two Iowa DNR pages contradict each other and neither is obviously stale, so reserve_until is deliberately absent. iowadnr.gov/places-go/state-parks/make-reservation/overnight-camping: 'The last day to make a camping reservation, if paying by credit/debit card, is 2 days prior to arrival.' iowadnr.gov/places-go/state-parks/make-reservation: 'The window for reserving campsites is 3 months in advance and up to the day of to the arrival date if paying by credit card.' The 2-day version matches the 48-hour rule reported by AWH. FCFS AFTER THE CUTOFF IS ALSO UNCONFIRMED: no official page found saying unreserved sites revert to first-come at the park. What IS documented is that all campers must register, and that Fort Defiance and Preparation Canyon are walk-in only year-round. Resolve by phone (1-877-427-2757) before trusting either.

booking.source: https://www.iowadnr.gov/places-go/state-parks/make-reservation/overnight-camping and https://www.iowadnr.gov/media/7065/download (State Park Rules & Reservation Information) - see note, the two disagree

booking.note: Same-day booking closes at 17:00, but only SOME parks accept it - verbatim: 'Same day reservations are allowed at a limited number of parks through the call center and website until 5 pm.' Which parks is not published, so reserve_until is absent at the agency level and belongs on the entries once known. FCFS does exist statewide: 'Walk-in guests at parks and forests can request any non-reserved sites', with named first-come areas at Hart-Miller Island and Green Ridge State Forest (self-registration). Weekend minimum runs Memorial Day through Labor Day and must be Thu/Fri, Fri/Sat or Sat/Sun; holiday weekends need Fri/Sat/Sun. No non-resident surcharge found.

A Green Key card is required to use the reservation system at all: 'The Green Key card is also required to access the online reservation system for camping and marina reservations.' A non-resident therefore cannot book online without first buying one - see fees.prereq_pass.

prereq_pass.name: Suffolk County Non-Resident Reservation Green Key

fees.note: Family camping base rates per night, cash: Resident $18 in season (Apr 1-Oct 31) and $9 off season (Nov 1-Mar 31); Non-resident $36 and $18 - exactly double, hence the multiplier. nightly_low/high hold the RESIDENT base. Site-tier fees are extra and not in surcharges because they have no cross-agency equivalent: Premier $22, Tier I $11, Tier II $5 per night. premium_site $4 is the Flagship Park fee and applies only at Smith Point, Cupsogue, Shinnecock East and Montauk - NOT Indian Island. A $3 registration fee applies on top of the $10 non-refundable reservation fee. Green Key prices: Resident $30 valid 3 years; Non-Resident Reservation Key $50 valid 1 year; Non-Resident VIP $200 valid 1 year, which buys resident rates (worth it only above ~30 nights).

min_stay.season: Memorial Day weekend - Labor Day weekend

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Most campsites in Pennsylvania state parks can be reserved 11 months in advance to noon of the day of arrival.' Minimum stay: 'During the summer season (Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend), campsites can be reserved for a minimum stay of one night (Sunday - Friday), and two nights if reserving a Saturday' - so the two-night rule is triggered by SATURDAY specifically, not by Friday, unlike IN/MD/IA. Outside summer there is no minimum. Strong walk-up: 'Unreserved sites are available on a first-come, first-served basis. If park employee is unavailable, read posted instructions, check the site availability listing, and then proceed to an available campsite and set up. The appropriate fee must be paid to a park employee or deposited in a supplied honor system envelope before setting up on a campsite.' Max stay is 14 consecutive nights Memorial Day-Labor Day and 21 the rest of the year; max_stay_nights holds the stricter camping-season figure.

fees.note: NON-RESIDENT RATE UNRESOLVED for state PARK campsites - no official page found stating one, so nonresident is absent rather than guessed. What IS published is a state FOREST rate, which is a different program: 'Motorized roadside, hike-in roadside, equestrian, and rustic campsites can be reserved for a fee of $10.00 a night for Pennsylvania residents and $15.00 a night for non-residents.' Do not apply that to state park campgrounds.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Campsites may be reserved up until 2 p.m. on the date of arrival' and 'Overnight accommodations, picnic shelters and some meeting facilities are available for reservations up to 11 months in advance.' FCFS NOT CONFIRMED - neither the reservations page nor the FAQ says whether an unreserved site can be taken on arrival, so fcfs is absent. Max stay is '14 nights in a 30-day period in any one park', which is not the same as 14 CONSECUTIVE nights; max_stay_nights approximates it. No weekend or holiday minimum stay found.

fees.note: The non-resident difference is NOT flat - it scales with site type: standard $27 resident / $32 non-resident (+$5), electric & water $37/$43 (+$6), full hookup $41-43/$48-50 (+$7-8). nonresident.amount holds the +$5 that applies to the standard site nightly_low describes; AN RV SITE WITH HOOKUPS SHOULD USE $7-8, so a cost estimate for a hookup site understates by up to $3/night if it uses the stored figure. Left as a single number deliberately rather than adding a range shape for one agency - revisit if a second state prices it this way. surcharges are derived from the resident rates ($37-$27, $43-$27). 'A $5 non-refundable transaction fee and applicable Virginia sales tax will be added to all fees.' Rates effective 5/12/2025.

season.note: 'Most campgrounds are open from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December; primitive sites are available year-round.' The dates FLOAT with the weekday, so 03-01/12-07 is an approximation of the widest span - check the individual park before relying on an edge date.

booking.note: DELIBERATELY THIN - federal is the one ownership where an agency default helps LEAST, and treating it like a state row would be the most expensive mistake in the registry (3,738 entries). Federal camping policy is set per FACILITY, not per agency: the 6-month rolling window at 10:00 ET is the recreation.gov standard, but group sites often open 12 months out and some BLM/USFS facilities use 14- or 30-day windows, and FCFS varies campground by campground - many USACE and USFS sites are entirely first-come. So fcfs and min_stay are absent here on purpose rather than defaulted. The right instrument for federal entries is the per-facility recreation.gov availability walk (docs/campground-schema.md phase 4), which answers season and FCFS from the calendar itself; this row exists only to supply the handful of facts that really are agency-wide. Note the doc's estimate of '3,738 entries from ~6-10 rows' was optimistic for exactly this reason.

fees.note: No resident/non-resident distinction exists on federal land.

discounts.note: America the Beautiful Senior and Access passes, per NPS: 'The Senior Pass may provide a 50 percent discount on some amenity fees charged for facilities and services such as camping, swimming, boat launch, and specialized interpretive services', honored by NPS, USFWS, USFS, BLM, Bureau of Reclamation and USACE. NOTE THE AGENCY'S OWN HEDGE - 'may' and 'some'. The discount is real and worth asking about at any federally operated campground, but it is discretionary per site, so treat this as 'ask', not 'guaranteed'. The standard $80 Annual Pass carries NO camping discount, which is a common and expensive assumption.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/articles/list/tips-for-making-campsite-reservations-at-popular-locations/281 (6-month rolling window); facility-level variance observed across BLM/USFS listings

booking.note: Verbatim: 'You have until 9 p.m. on a given day to book a campsite for that night' - among the latest same-day cutoffs found, second only to Indiana's 11pm. Minimum stay: 'On holiday weekends, a two-night minimum stay is required. This requirement is lifted within 7 days of arrival' - the same waiver shape as Indiana but a 7-day window instead of 3, and unlike Indiana the waiver DOES cover the holiday rule, because the holiday rule is the only one. Cabins are excluded: their 2-night minimum 'cannot be lifted, even if you are booking it within 7 days of arrival'. Walk-up sites exist but are identifiable only in the booking UI - 'An X means that the site is not available to book online - this would show up if the site has been designated as a walk-up only site' - so fcfs is 'some_sites' and which ones is not published as data. Max stay is 14 consecutive nights within any 30-day period. A secondary source said reservations must be made 1 day ahead; the agency's own page contradicts that and wins. Booking window not stated on the agency page (a secondary source says 6 months), so window_opens_days is absent.

fees.note: $3 per night per site non-refundable service fee; $6 cancellation fee; $6 transfer fee for same-day changes. As of 2025-05-01, tent sites $20-30 and full-hookup RV sites $45. No non-resident rate difference found.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Reservations at state parks may be made up to 13 months in advance' - the longest window found so far, against 6-11 months elsewhere. Minimum stay is unusual in applying YEAR-ROUND rather than to weekends: 'Cabin and campsite rentals are typically accepted for a two-night minimum, however, during busier periods, minimum stays may be increased at some parks.' Note 'typically' and 'some parks' - the agency hedges, so treat the 2-night rule as the default and not a certainty, and no waiver is published. Inside a day of arrival the CHANNEL changes rather than closing: 'Reservations requested less than one (1) day in advance of check-in must be made directly through the park' - so same-day booking is possible but not online, which is why reserve_until is absent (nothing shuts) and why a late arrival should call the park. FCFS is not addressed anywhere on the agency site.

fees.note: Campsite cancellation ladder: '60 + days away - no charge; 15 - 59 days away - $10 Administrative Fee; 4-14 days - 1st night's stay; 3 days or less - no refund.' Out-of-state seniors/disabled get discounts at specific parks only; no general non-resident rate difference.

booking.note: Delaware publishes very little of what this schema wants. Confirmed: 'Camping is permitted for a maximum of 14 days within a 21-day period per park', one mobile unit plus one tent (or two tents) and one vehicle per site, and an 18-day change freeze from the day the reservation is made, during which arrival dates cannot be moved and reservations cannot be transferred. NOT PUBLISHED on the agency site: the advance booking window, any same-day cutoff, any minimum stay, and whether unreserved sites can be walked up to. Those stay absent rather than being borrowed from a neighbouring state. Only 5 entries inherit this row, so the cost of the gap is small.

discounts.note: Delaware scales the America the Beautiful Access Pass discount BY RESIDENCY, which no other agency checked does: Delaware residents holding the pass get 20% off camping, non-residents holding the same pass get 10%. So the flag is true either way but the value is not - a VA family gets the smaller half.

booking.note: UNCONFIRMED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE - floridastateparks.org returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so everything here comes from search-surfaced summaries of it rather than the page itself. Verify before relying on it. Florida is the only agency found that varies the BOOKING WINDOW by residency rather than the price: residents may reserve up to 11 months ahead, non-residents up to 10, so a Virginia family is bidding for the same sites a month behind every Floridian. window_opens_days holds the RESIDENT figure, matching the convention that stored values are the resident base; a non-resident should read 300. Residents are also reported to be able to book same-day up to 1 p.m., with no equivalent stated for non-residents - if that asymmetry is real it matters more than the price for a late arrival, so it is the first thing to check. Reported fees: $6.70 non-refundable service fee, $17.75 cancellation, plus the first night if cancelling on the day of arrival.

booking.source: https://www.floridastateparks.org/reservation-information and .../early-access-camping-florida-residents - NOT directly retrievable (403); figures are secondary

booking.note: Six months ahead. Max stay is 15 nights during peak season (May 15 - Sept 15), after which a 5-night break is required before returning to the SAME park - a cumulative rule the schema stores only as the nightly cap. No minimum stay found, and walk-in availability is not addressed on the agency pages checked.

fees.note: The Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to ALL state park and forest campgrounds, so it is unavoidable, not optional. Residents buy it with vehicle registration at $15/year (two years $29); non-residents pay $40/year or $11/DAY. Which is cheaper turns purely on trip length - four nights of day passes ($44) already exceeds the annual one, so a family visiting Michigan even once for a week should buy the annual. Prices effective 2026-01-01. Motorcycles $7, commercial vehicles $22. entrance holds the annual figures because that is how the passport is sold; the $11 day rate is the alternative, not the default.

booking.source: https://midnrreservations.com/ and Michigan DNR camping guidance

booking.note: Verbatim: 'The public can reserve the highly sought-after campsites and lodging six months in advance from the current date', with 'Each new date opens at 8 a.m. PST' - a rolling daily release, so a sought-after site is won at 8am six months out rather than by planning earlier. Walk-up survives: 'Yes, you may still enjoy walk-up camping. Some sites will remain first-come, first-served.' Which sites is not published. No minimum stay stated at the agency level, and no resident/non-resident distinction of any kind - notable given how many states have one, and it makes California one of the few where a Virginia family pays exactly what a Californian does.

fees.note: $8.25 non-refundable reservation fee and $8.25 cancellation fee (both since 2024-08-01). No non-resident surcharge and no resident/non-resident entrance split.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Parks that use the reservation system no longer offer walk-in campsites. NOTE: Jesse Owens State Park is the only park that offers first-come, first-served camping with on-site registration.' So fcfs is 'never' at the agency level with exactly ONE named exception, which carries its own entry-level override. 'Reservations for campsites can be made as late as the day of your desired arrival' - no published clock time, so reserve_until holds end-of-day; do not read 23:59 as a quoted figure. Minimum stay: 'The minimum stay for regular weekend reservations is 2 nights. On Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends, the minimum stay is 3 nights', with 'no minimum for camping ... made for Sunday-Thursday nights'. The waiver is 'If it is within 7 days of your desired stay and campsites are available, reservations will be accepted for 1 night' - stated under Minimum Stay generally, AFTER both rules and without the carve-out Indiana makes explicit, so it is applied to both here. That reading is an inference, not a quote; check before relying on it for a holiday weekend. Campsites 6 months ahead, cabins 12.

fees.note: 'Applicable taxes plus a $6.50 reservation fee are added to every reservation.' No non-resident rate difference found.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'All parks are reservation only.' Colorado abolished walk-up camping outright, which makes it one of the worst states in the database to roll into at 7pm without a booking - there is no fallback at all, unlike Pennsylvania's honor-envelope system or Maryland's any-unreserved-site rule. 'A reservation can be made no more than six months before your arrival date', released at midnight Mountain Time. No published same-day cutoff, so reserve_until is absent. No minimum stay found.

fees.note: 'Daily park entrance fees of $10-11 apply in addition to camping fees, or a valid annual pass must be displayed' - so, like Indiana and Michigan, the campsite price is not the whole price. Unlike them, Colorado does NOT split the vehicle fee by residency, so resident and nonresident are recorded the same; the $10-11 range is by park. Nightly sites run $13-41 by type and season.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, July 4 (when it falls Fri-Mon), Labor Day

booking.note: ILLINOIS DOCUMENTS THE PATTERN IOWA'S OWN PAGES ONLY HINT AT, and clearly: 'reservations must be made three days before the campsite is needed' AND 'Most campgrounds have first-come, first-served sites; please contact the park for availability'. So booking shuts three days out and walk-up takes over - the same mechanism reported for Iowa, here stated unambiguously by the agency. Worth knowing when reading the Iowa row, whose two official pages contradict each other on exactly this. Minimum stay applies only to named holidays: 'Memorial Day, Fourth of July (if July 4th falls on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday or Monday) and Labor Day weekends require a two night minimum stay. Some facilities will require a three night minimum stay for Columbus Day.' Season: 'Most campsites may be reserved from May 1 through October 31. Some parks accept reservations year-round.' Reservations moved to an updated exploremoreil.com platform on 2026-05-01, and an administrative-rule/fee change is dated 2026-08-31 for 2027 - re-check this row before the 2027 season.

fees.note: 'The reservation fee is $5.00, plus the entire camping fee for each camp site reserved. This $5.00 reservation fee is non-refundable.' No non-resident rate difference found. A 2027 camping-fee change was published 2026-08-31.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'All campsites in Minnesota state parks and recreation areas now require a reservation before they may be occupied', and the DNR is explicit that this was a deliberate abolition: 'No more arriving on a Friday hoping to stay at a first-come, first-served site, only to find there isn't one available!' BUT unlike Colorado, the same-day path works and is free: 'Reserve a site online Friday morning and be camping in it that same night!' So fcfs is never while a late arrival is still perfectly possible - the two facts must be read together, and a search that treats 'no FCFS' as 'no late arrival' would wrongly exclude every Minnesota park. The 120-day window is the shortest found (against 180 typical and South Carolina's 395). State FORESTS are a separate system and DO keep first-come sites; this row covers state parks and recreation areas only.

fees.note: 'Overnight guests need a state park vehicle permit in addition to a camping or lodging reservation' - $7 daily, or $35 for a year-round permit good 12 months from purchase. No residency split, so both sides are recorded the same. Five nights of day permits exceeds the annual.

booking.note: Five months ahead for camping, 30 days for day passes. Minimum stay is triggered by ANY of Friday, Saturday or Sunday being included - broader than Pennsylvania (Saturday only) and stated to vary by park, so treat it as the default rather than a certainty. No waiver published. Walk-up availability is not addressed on the pages checked, so fcfs is absent.

fees.note: Texas charges entrance PER PERSON per day rather than per vehicle - the only agency checked that does - 'unless you hold a Texas State Parks Pass'. The amount varies by park and is not recorded here because there is no single figure; check the park. That distinction matters for a family: a per-person gate fee scales with headcount where Indiana's and Michigan's per-vehicle ones do not. Campsites run $10-35 by type and season.

booking.note: The strongest walk-up wording found anywhere: 'Campsites that cannot be reserved are offered on a first come, first served basis. In many cases, reservable sites that have not been booked can also be used on a first come, first served basis.' Booking shuts early - 'most reservations can only be made up until 8 pm two days before your arrival date' - but with a caveat no other agency has: 'Parks that have internet connectivity accept reservations right up until your planned arrival date.' So the cutoff is a function of whether the park has a signal, not of policy, and reserve_until holds the conservative two-day figure. THE WINDOW CHANGED FOR 2026: three months, down from four; anything citing four months is stale. Released 7am Pacific daily. Statutory holiday weekends need three nights. MAX STAY IS PER CALENDAR YEAR, not per visit - 'At most parks, you can stay a maximum of 14 nights each calendar year in total (consecutive or non-consecutive)', and seven at sWiWs and Porteau Cove. That is a different kind of limit from everywhere else in this registry and max_stay_nights cannot express it; read the note.

fees.note: Reservation fee '$6 per campsite per night, to a maximum of $18 per site (plus tax)'; phone adds a $5 per-transaction surcharge. Cancelling more than seven days out refunds camping fees but never the transaction fees. No out-of-province rate difference. NOTE on rating.price_tier for Canadian entries: the imported RV Life tier is computed on nominal dollars with no CAD conversion, so Canadian parks sit roughly one level high - see docs/campground-schema.md 4.3.

booking.note: 'Individual Campsites: 90 day booking window', advancing one day each morning at 9 a.m. MT; group and comfort camping open at 180 days. 'Campers can book a maximum of 10 consecutive nights per reservation' - up to 16 at one site by stacking bookings - and five nights in a group area. First-come camping exists as its own category on the Alberta Parks site but the FAQ does not state the rule, so fcfs is absent rather than guessed. No same-day cutoff published, hence no reserve_until. No minimum stay found and no out-of-province rate difference. A reservation booked on the first day of the window is frozen to date changes for 31 days.

fees.note: The reservation FAQ names only 'non-refundable administrative fees' without amounts, so reservation_fee is absent. See the BC row's note on Canadian rating.price_tier being roughly one level high.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Reservations can be made up to 9:00 pm on your day of arrival' - equal to North Carolina and second only to Indiana's 11pm, and much the most generous of the three provinces here (BC effectively shuts two days out). 'Reservations are accepted up to five months in advance', released 7am ET. Maximum stay is the longest in the registry: 'The maximum stay on a campsite at all other parks and during off-season is twenty-three consecutive nights', reduced to 7-14 nights in peak season (July 1 to Labour Day Saturday) at the busiest parks such as Algonquin and Pinery - so max_stay_nights holds the off-season figure and a July booking should assume less. No minimum stay is published. Walk-in availability is not addressed in the rules, so fcfs is absent.

fees.note: 'A non-refundable reservation fee is required for all reservations' with no amount published in the rules; cancellation penalties live on a separate page. See the BC row's note on Canadian rating.price_tier.

min_stay.season: stays May 15 - Oct 31 BOOKED before May 15

booking.note: Reservations are mandatory - 'Campers must make a reservation before setting up on any site' - but same-day booking is allowed: 'Camping reservations are required and can be made on the same day of your arrival or up to 11 months before your planned occupancy date.' No clock time is published, so reserve_until holds end-of-day. THE 2-NIGHT MINIMUM KEYS ON WHEN YOU BOOK, NOT WHEN YOU STAY, which no other agency here does: 'reservations booked before May 15 for stays between May 15 and Oct. 31 require a minimum 2-night reservation', while sites still available after May 15 may be booked for one night. So it never binds a late booker, and a one-night search must NOT exclude Wisconsin on the strength of it. Holiday weekends need 3 nights. Remote forest areas may have non-reservable camping; standard park sites do not.

fees.note: 'Nonresident campers will pay $15 per night in addition to the standard campsite fee' - THE LARGEST per-night non-resident surcharge in the registry, three times New York's $5 and roughly double Virginia's worst case. On a four-night stay that is $60 before the campsite is paid for. A vehicle admission pass is required on top (daily, or a 12-month pass); resident/non-resident amounts for the pass were not published on the page checked.

booking.note: THE CLEANEST HANDOFF IN THE REGISTRY, and the model the others should be read against: 'Campers can book a same-day reservation until 2 p.m. on their intended day of arrival' and 'First come, first served camping is still available for unreserved sites after 2:30 p.m.' Two mechanisms with a published boundary and a half-hour of slack between them, effective 2025-03-24 when same-day booking expanded from a few parks to all reservable campgrounds. Reservable season is May 15 - Sept 15 at most parks, some year-round or wider; outside it, and in winter when loops close, sites may be first-come anyway. From 2025-08-19 a reservation cannot exceed 10 nights, nor push the camper past a 90-night annual total - max_stay_nights holds the per-reservation cap, not the annual one.

fees.note: A Discover Pass is the state's vehicle access pass; its interaction with camping fees was not confirmed on the pages checked, so no entrance figures are recorded.

booking.note: 180 days for camping, a year for cabins and lodges. Walk-up is explicit and has a registration path: 'Non-reservable campsites are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis' and 'first-come, first-served campers must register at the entrance booth or office, or at a self-registration drop box' - the same honour-system shape as Pennsylvania. fcfs is 'some_sites' rather than 'always' because the wording covers NON-RESERVABLE sites specifically and does not say unbooked reservable ones may be taken. No minimum stay for standard sites (cabins need two nights). No same-day cutoff published.

fees.note: 'A Motor Vehicle Park Entry Permit is required on all licensed vehicles entering any state park, state recreation area or state historical park' - so, as in Indiana, Michigan, Colorado and Minnesota, the campsite price is not the whole price. Resident/non-resident amounts were not published on the pages checked, so entrance is absent rather than guessed.

booking.note: 'Reservations are not required for campsites, but are highly recommended' - one of the few agencies left where turning up is a supported way to camp rather than a fallback. 90 days ahead, released 7am CT / 6am MT, except Custer State Park which opens a full year out. The recommendation is not idle: most summer weekend sites go within a week of the window opening, so fcfs 'always' describes the policy, not the odds.

fees.note: 'Camping fees do not include entrance fees, which are required year-round and in most areas' - an annual entrance licence can be bought ahead online and mailed. Resident/non-resident amounts were not published on the pages checked.

booking.note: Verbatim on 19 of the 23 park camping pages: 'Reservations may be made for no less than two consecutive nights on weekends (Friday and Saturday) or one night Sunday through Thursday' - so the pair Friday+Saturday triggers it, unlike PA where Saturday alone does. NOT universal, and the exceptions run both ways: Lost River says 'Reservations may be made any night' (no minimum at all), while Camp Creek applies it only 'during the season on weekends starting on the Thursday before Memorial Day and ends the day after Labor Day'. The rule here is the majority default; a one-night weekend booking is worth checking on the park's own page. max_stay_nights is from the legislative rule (58CSR32 s2.4): 'The rental period for any campsite may not exceed 14 consecutive nights' - 'except that, after Labor Day until May 1st of the following year, the area superintendent, at his or her discretion, may rent campsites for longer periods when vacant campsites are available.' WINDOW UNRESOLVED: no official page publishes how far ahead booking opens. Every park page says only 'Campsites may be reserved anytime online, by phone, or at the campground office', rates and the calendar live inside the Inntopia booking engine, and the 12-months figure in circulation is a third-party aggregator's - window_opens_days is absent rather than guessed. FCFS NOT CONFIRMED: no campsite on any of the 23 pages is offered first-come (the only 'first-come' text found anywhere is Stonewall's boat MOORING POSTS), and two parks say the opposite - Seneca: 'Before occupying any campsite, campers must have a paid reservation and all sites are reservable', Tygart: 'All campsites are reservable.' Against that, 58CSR32 s2.1 still contemplates paying 'in person at the campground check-in station or park office'. Beware the pre-online park brochures and campground applications still served from wvstateparks.com: they describe held-back FCFS sites and say reservations 'must be made at least two (2) days prior to arrival', which the current system contradicts. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon; s2.6 'Campsites shall be vacated by 12:00 noon'. Cancellation: 'Reservations canceled at least 60 days prior to arrival may request a refund for the deposit paid', credit-only inside 60 days, nothing inside 7.

fees.note: NO RATES PUBLISHED. Scanned all 23 park camping pages: not one dollar figure appears on any of them, and there is no statewide camping-rates page - the numbers exist only inside the booking engine (book.wvstateparks.com, Inntopia), per park and per site type. nightly_low/high are absent rather than sampled from one park. NON-RESIDENT RATE: none found on any official page, so nonresident is absent, not zero. The only residency-linked term West Virginia publishes is a discount, not a surcharge: 58CSR32 s2.13, 'West Virginia residents who are totally and permanently disabled are entitled to a 50 percent discount on campground rental fees from the day after Labor Day until four days prior to Memorial Day only', on application for a permanent campground discount card. Reservation/transaction fee not published either; full payment is taken at booking.

season.note: Per park and undated, so opens/closes are absent. 14 of the 23 camping pages say the campground is 'open spring through fall, weather permitting' without naming a date at either end; six run year-round (Camp Creek, Panther, Pipestem, Twin Falls, Stonewall's Briar Point, and Blackwater Falls sites 1-30, where 'Some facilities on these sites are limited after October 31, until April 1'). Derive a real season per entry from the park page or the booking calendar.

booking.note: No reservations: WMA camping is temporary dispersed primitive camping in previously cleared spots, first come. Instead a CAMPING AUTHORIZATION is required ('a camping authorization (no cost) is required to camp on WMA's'), got from any license agent or Go Outdoors Virginia under 'Special Licenses'. It sets a start and end date for the trip and 'Up to six people can camp under the same authorization' (more if all one household), so it is ONE PER CAMPING PARTY, not per person. Free now; $10 from 2026-10-01. Stay limit is '14 consecutive nights ... (no more than 14 nights in any 28-day period)', and camping is allowed only 'when occupants are engaged in authorized activities'. No camping on or within 300 ft of a boat ramp, fishing lake or other facility; none at all at Guinea Marsh or Land's End WMAs. DWR warns 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers' and some WMAs bar travel trailers/RVs.

prereq_pass.name: WMA camping authorization, one per party of up to 6

fees.note: There is no camping fee; nightly 0 is the camping charge, not the cost of a night. The real cost is the DWR ACCESS PERMIT, required PER PERSON: 'Any person 17 years of age or older accessing a DWR Wildlife Management Area ... must have in possession' a Virginia hunting, freshwater fishing or trapping license, a Virginia boat registration, or an Access Permit. 16 and under are exempt. Daily $4/person; annual $23/person ($28 from 2026-10-01); a group daily permit is $26 for 1-12 people, bought and carried by the leader with a participant list. OVERNIGHT = BOTH DAYS: the FAQ says a daily permit is valid 'for the date of the Permit', and the permit must be in possession while on the property, so a one-night stay spans two dates and needs a daily permit dated for EACH (arrival and departure) - two adults, one night = $16. That is read from the wording; DWR does not state the overnight case explicitly (confirm at 1-866-721-6911). The annual permit pays for itself at ~6 visit-days per person. The camping authorization (booking note) is a separate, per-party document.
